correctness.rationale: From the formal WOM definition, every first-generation representative \(x\) must have an upward cone containing all four messages, so \(2^{3-\operatorname{wt}(x)}\ge4\) and \(\operatorname{wt}(x)\le1\). The four messages therefore force the four states of weight at most one. Pairwise comparison of their upward cones then forces \(111\) to share the label of \(000\) and each weight-two state to share the label of its complementary weight-one state. This proves exactly \(4!=24\) decoders. The converse is direct. A separate exhaustive verifier checks all \(65{,}536\) interpretation functions, the exact survivor set, the forced first states, and the \(16\) reachable second-write transition tables per decoder.

value.rationale: The \((4)^2/3\) construction is the motivating small WOM code in the foundational paper and is repeatedly reused as a canonical building block. The classification shows that its decoder is forced by monotone rewriting: there is one message-relabeling class, not a collection of unrelated optimal decoders. This is a natural complete equality classification of the smallest nontrivial four-message rewrite code, with a short structural proof and exhaustive independent check.
